title: Bellarmine: infused virtues still need daily remission
source_text: XXIX. Bellarminus vero non minus aperte significat quo sensu renatorum justitiam & sanctitatem perfectam & absolutam vocet, lib. 2. de Justif. cap. 13. nam ibi fatetur virtutes infusas, quibus fidelium justitia constat, ita suo quodam modo perfectas esse, ut quotidie magis ac magis perfici debeant. Et paulo post subjungit virtutem semel infusam egere quotidie nova remissione peccati. Justi enim, inquit, tametsi multa bona & justa opera faciunt, tamen saepe etiam labuntur in peccata levia & venialia. Capite vero sequenti justitiam habitualem, ita & non aliter perfectam esse asserit, ut per eam abso-lute, simpliciter, & proprie justi nominemur & simus. De justitia vero actuali sic loquitur, Quamvis aliquo modo sit imperfecta, propter admixtionem venialium delictorum, & egeat quotidiana remissione peccati; tamen, non propterea desinit esse vera justitia, & sua etiam quodam modo perfecta.
pass_a_gloss: But Bellarmine no less openly signifies in what sense he calls the righteousness and holiness of the regenerate perfect and absolute (book 2 on Justification, chapter 13): for there he confesses that the infused virtues of which the righteousness of believers consists are perfect in their own way in such a fashion that they ought daily to be more and more perfected. And a little later he adds that a virtue once infused needs daily a new remission of sin. For the just, he says, although they do many good and just works, yet often also fall into light and venial sins. And in the following chapter he asserts that habitual righteousness is perfect in this way and no other, that by it we are absolutely, simply, and properly named and are just. But of actual righteousness he speaks thus: Although it is in some way imperfect because of the admixture of venial faults, and needs daily remission of sin, yet it does not on that account cease to be true righteousness, and in its own way also perfect.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine: infused virtues are perfect in a mode yet must daily be perfected; they need daily remission of venials.
Habitual justice makes us just absolutely; actual justice is somehow imperfect by venial mixture.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1063.
